item.title: Windows and macOS in Docker in 2026: dockur/windows vs Docker-OSX vs Plain QEMU
item.description:
Windows and macOS in Docker in 2026: dockur/windows vs Docker-OSX vs Plain QEMU

A docker compose up that boots a licensed copy of Windows 11, hands you a browser-based console on port 8006, and lets you RDP into it — that is not a thought experiment anymore. Two projects with a combined 106,000+ GitHub stars have turned “foreign OS in a container” into a supported workflow. The catch is that the three approaches people actually use (dockur/windows, Docker-OSX, and raw QEMU) solve different problems, and two of them carry licensing obligations that will bite you in production.

item.title: Renode vs QEMU vs gem5 in 2026: Which Emulator Should Back Your Firmware Pipeline?
item.description: The weakest link in most embedded teams is not the compiler or the kernel — it is the physical board sitting on one engineer’s desk. One dev kit, one person flashing it, and a regression suite that only runs when somebody remembers to plug it in. Emulation fixes that, but the three obvious choices are not interchangeable: QEMU (13,753 GitHub stars) emulates fast enough to run a full Linux userspace, Renode (2,924 stars) models multi-node boards deterministically for CI, and gem5 (2,827 stars) trades speed for architectural fidelity you can publish papers about.
